entry.summary: There are two main members/types of storage in AWS Storage family, Uncle (block) and Aunty (object). Who storage information depending upon their nature and temperament. And you need to keep their nature in mind while trying to retrieve information from them. 😉 If you give any information (say 1GB) to uncle/block, he is easy to go guy. entry.title: SQL Cursor and Trigger Implementation
entry.summary:
In this post, we’ll explore two key SQL programming concepts: 🌀 1️⃣ Cursor: Display Employees with Salary Greater than 50,000 A cursor is used to process each record returned by a query, one row at a time. ✅ Step 1: Create a Cursor DECLARE emp_record emp_cursor%ROWTYPE;
BEGIN 🧠 Explanation: CURSOR emp_cursor IS → Defines the SQL query. emp_record emp_cursor%ROWTYPE → Declares a record to store fetched rows. OPEN, FETCH, CLOSE → Manage cursor operations. DBMS_OUTPUT.PUT_LINE → Displays each result. 🖥 Output: Employee: Arjun, Salary: 60000
⚡ 2️⃣ AFTER INSERT Trigger — Student Registration Audit A trigger automatically performs an action when a specified database event occurs. ✅ Step 2: Create AFTER INSERT Trigger CREATE OR REPLACE TRIGGER trg_student_insert 🧠 Explanation: AFTER INSERT ON Students → Trigger runs after a new record is inserted. :NEW → Refers to the new row being added. Student_Audit Table → Logs inserted student records automatically. ✅ Step 3: Test the Trigger INSERT INTO Students (StudentID, StudentName) 🖥 Output: Trigger TRG_STUDENT_INSERT compiled And a new log entry will appear in the Student_Audit table 🎯
🏁 Summary Feature Description Example Cursor Used for row-by-row processing Displays employees earning > ₹50,000 💡 Conclusion Cursors and Triggers are essential for database automation and record handling. @santhoshnc sir for guiding and supporting me..
